boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of California-Berkeley, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-first loop of campus landmarks, a quiet indoor pause, and two ways to start connecting with Berkeley life.

cards.title: 1. Start at the Koret Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: California Memorial Stadium
cards.notes: Pick up the campus orientation here, then use the visitor resources to choose a self-guided route that fits the time you have.
cards.short_summary: A practical starting point for getting your bearings on the first morning.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley Visitor Services lists the Koret Visitor Center at California Memorial Stadium and offers self-guided campus tours.
cards.access_notes: Visitor Services publishes separate operating hours; check its current page before going.

cards.title: 2. See California Memorial Stadium
cards.subtitle: Goldman Plaza, by the visitor center
cards.notes: Pause on Goldman Plaza to identify the stadium and its surrounding campus buildings before continuing toward the academic core.
cards.short_summary: A landmark-oriented stop immediately beside the visitor center.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley states that the Koret Visitor Center is on Goldman Plaza inside the gates of historic California Memorial Stadium.
cards.access_notes: The Visitor Services directions page identifies this as the visitor-center location; event-day access conditions can vary.

cards.title: 3. Find the Campanile
cards.subtitle: Central campus landmark
cards.notes: Use the tower as a visual waypoint while you cross campus, and take an exterior photo from the surrounding esplanade.
cards.short_summary: A simple landmark stop that makes the rest of campus easier to navigate.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley Visitor Services identifies the Campanile, also called Sather Tower, as a campus attraction and a 307-foot clock and bell tower.
cards.access_notes: This card is for viewing the exterior; verify tower-entry details separately if you plan to go inside.

cards.title: 4. Take a daylight break on Memorial Glade
cards.subtitle: Between Doe Library and the campus core
cards.notes: Walk the edge of the glade, locate the memorial pool at its northwest corner, and pause before heading indoors.
cards.short_summary: An open-space reset with a documented campus memorial nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley describes Memorial Glade as a major green open space for reflection and informal leisure, with a memorial pool at its northwest corner.
cards.source_title: Memorial Glade - University of California, Berkeley
cards.access_notes: Use normal daylight awareness and follow any posted campus-event instructions.

cards.title: 5. Step into Doe Library
cards.subtitle: Doe Memorial Library
cards.notes: Enter during posted open hours, orient yourself to the service desk, and save the library page for current access details.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing library stop for learning the central study landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley Library says Doe is open to the public and that visitors need no identification, registration, pass, or prior arrangements to visit.
cards.access_notes: Hours change by date; consult the library's live hours table. Some services and rooms have eligibility limits.

cards.title: 6. Read or listen in Morrison Library
cards.subtitle: 101 Doe Library
cards.notes: If it is open, leave laptops packed and spend a few minutes with the reading room’s books, magazines, or listening space.
cards.short_summary: A quieter, laptop-free reading-room stop within Doe Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley Library describes Morrison Library as open to the public and laptop-free, with seating for reading and a collection of books, magazines, and music.
cards.access_notes: Check the library's current hours before visiting; a UC Berkeley library card is needed to check out circulating materials.

cards.title: 7. Walk through Sproul Plaza
cards.subtitle: Near Sproul Hall
cards.notes: Cross the plaza at a relaxed pace, notice current student tables or notices if present, and keep the space clear for campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A central public plaza tied to Berkeley's student-life and free-expression history.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley Visitor Services calls Sproul Plaza the epicenter of student life and notes its role in the 1964–65 Free Speech Movement.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is an active campus space; follow posted directions and do not obstruct tables, rallies, or demonstrations.

cards.title: 8. Pass through Sather Gate
cards.subtitle: Between Sproul Plaza and central campus
cards.notes: Look up at the eight bas-relief panels, then continue through the gate as you connect the plaza with the campus interior.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic gateway and clear transition point in the walking sequence.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley identifies Sather Gate as a campus point of interest, notes its history as the formal south entrance, and describes its eight bas-relief panels.
cards.source_title: Sather Gate - University of California, Berkeley
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor pedestrian landmark; remain attentive to surrounding foot traffic and campus activity.

cards.title: 9. Check the Berkeley Art Studio schedule
cards.subtitle: MLK Jr. Building, Student Union
cards.notes: Browse the current class offerings and registration details, then decide whether a future drawing, ceramics, or photography class fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A concrete way to explore creative classes open to the campus and local community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Berkeley Art Studio says registration is open to the public and lists classes in ceramics, photography, drawing, painting, design, printmaking, and textile arts.
cards.source_title: Welcome to the Berkeley Art Studio
cards.access_notes: The studio lists weekend hours of noon–5 p.m.; classes require registration and fees vary by offering.

cards.title: 10. Tour your fitness options at the RSF
cards.subtitle: 2301 Bancroft Way
cards.notes: Review the facility offerings and membership rules, then plan a future workout or activity after confirming that your access is active.
cards.short_summary: A documented overview stop for Berkeley's main recreation and fitness facility.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley Recreation & Wellbeing describes the RSF as its largest fitness center and says facility access is for Recreation & Wellbeing members.
cards.access_notes: Present proof of Recreation & Wellbeing membership or purchase at the front desk; consult the RSF hours page before visiting.
